questions.prompt: Which small input best exposes an accidental square-board assumption?

options.label: 2 rows and 3 columns.
3 rows and 3 columns.
1 row and 1 column.

questions.explanation: A non-square board requires independent bounds. Square and single-cell cases can pass even when the column loop incorrectly uses the row count.

questions.prompt: With 3 columns, what are the coordinates of flat index 5?

options.label: Row 1, column 2.
Row 2, column 1.
Row 1, column 1.

questions.explanation: Integer division 5 // 3 gives row 1 and remainder 5 % 3 gives column 2. Dividing by the row count swaps the contract and fails rectangular inputs.

options.label: Both rows begin with 9.
Only the first row changes.
Python rejects the assignment.

questions.explanation: List multiplication repeats references to the same inner list. Allocate each inner list in a comprehension to preserve row independence; nested assignment itself is legal.

questions.prompt: What is the correct statement about useRef?

options.label: Changing ref.current does not itself schedule a render.
Changing ref.current always rerenders its component.
A ref is a memoized function.

questions.explanation: A ref holds a mutable value across renders without triggering one when changed. Visible board dimensions belong in state. useCallback caches a function definition.

questions.prompt: Which description distinguishes useMemo from useCallback?

options.label: useMemo caches a calculation result; useCallback caches a function definition.
Both are required to render arrays.
Both guarantee a component never rerenders.

questions.explanation: Memoization is a performance tool, not a correctness requirement. Neither hook stops all rerenders, and a small coordinate grid can compute directly during rendering.

questions.prompt: When would coordinate keys become the wrong identity?

options.label: When cells represent entities that reorder independently of positions.
Whenever the board has more than one row.
Whenever a component rerenders.

questions.explanation: Keys connect sibling identity across renders. Coordinates fit stateless positions, but movable entity records need stable entity IDs so state follows the record.

questions.prompt: Does generating rows lazily remove the O(rows × columns) rendered-cell cost?

options.label: No; materializing and rendering every cell still costs that work.
Yes; generators make all rendering constant time.
Yes; keys eliminate the cell traversal.

questions.explanation: A generator can avoid building some intermediates, but this interface ultimately materializes every row and cell. Keys guide identity rather than eliminating traversal.

questions.prompt: Order these baseline implementation steps by dependency. Each step prepares the next.
questions.explanation: Define the input and state rules, implement the dependent transformation, then validate the result. Reversing this order risks testing a UI before its rules or input identity are defined. This is one rehearsal sequence; other engineering workflows can work.
